newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tokyo stocks end lower, other Asia markets gain.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end lower, other Asia markets gain.

text.p: Japan's Nikkei share index closed below 20,500 for the first time in six weeks on Thursday, while Hong Kong stocks put in a strong showing for the second consecutive day.
The Nikkei 225 closed beneath the 20,500 line for the first time since September 12. Brokers said futures-linked selling weighed heavily on the average while most investors were sidelined.
The Nikkei average fell 214.81 points, or 1.04 percent, to 20,466.86.
"Right before the market closed, bouts of index selling emerged, dragging the average below the 20,500 level," one broker said.
Investment trusts were not in a mood to buy and in the afternoon, market participants who had bought earlier in anticipation of rises moved to square their positions, sending the benchmark lower.

"Once the Nikkei 225 tumbles below the 20,500 level, technical charts strongly signal a rebound," said Dai-ichi Securities analyst Masayuki Matsumoto. "It may be difficult to see one tomorrow, but sometime next week the index should spring up slightly."
Investors in Hong Kong were still bullish from Wednesday's gains, although there were worries about the impact of upcoming U.S. economic data, brokers said.
The Hang Seng index rose 72.09 points to 12,477.56 after slipping into negative territory early in the session.

"On the one hand, local shares just followed yesterday's rebound and continue to fare quite well, but on the other hand I think investors are still concerned about the U.S. figures," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
September U.S. personal income and consumption data are due on Thursday and the October U.S. jobs report on Friday.

"I think the market has made its move for this week and I think it is going to sit around and wait for some of the data coming out," said Alan Hutcheson, director of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Australian shares closed firmer after a late buying spree. The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 13.5 points higher at 2,350.2, well off its intra-session low of 2,329.3.
Brokers said low turnover indicated that investors remained non-committal ahead of next week's Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) board meeting and the imminent U.S. elections.
South Korean stocks closed almost flat, putting an end to an eight-day falling streak on the view that the market has bottomed out, brokers said.
"The market's free-fall seems to be halted. The view that the market is near the bottom will promote bargain hunting on Friday," said Lee Ha-yong, a broker at Hyundai Securities.
The composite stock index closed 0.5 of a point higher at a provisional 757.59. Brokers said lingering hopes of lower interest rates in November would help buoy sentiment.
Taiwan's stock market was closed for a national holiday and reopens on Friday.
Gold bullion tumbled in Hong Kong to finish at $379.20/70 an ounce against New York's $380.15/55, dealers said.
SIMEX December crude futures rebounded, trading at $23.70 per barrel, up 13 cents from London's settlement on Wednesday.
At 1115 GMT, the dollar traded at 113.57/3.62 yen and 1.5107/12 marks.
